exposure: Maternal fat intake (omega-3 polyunsaturated fat, omega-6 polyunsaturated fat, saturated fatty acids) during first and second trimesters
cohort: The study included 96 mothers with uncomplicated full-term pregnancies, most of whom had a normal body mass index (BMI), participating in Project Viva.
finding: Early prenatal fat intake, particularly omega-6 and omega-3 polyunsaturated fats during the first trimester, was associated with differential DNA methylation at the IGF2 and H19 loci in cord blood.
